title: Set default Admin credentials (Rushikesh / 123)

requirements.text: Seed/set the default Admin account credentials to username "Rushikesh" and password "123" in the backend’s admin-managed username/password authentication system, ensuring the account has the Admin role and can be used to sign in after deployment/upgrade.

quotes: make Admin username  as - Rushikesh Passoword - 123

acceptanceCriteria: On a fresh deployment, an Admin account exists with username "Rushikesh" and password "123".
The seeded Admin account has role "Admin" and is able to authenticate successfully.

If the canister is upgraded and an Admin user already exists, the upgrade does not unintentionally overwrite existing admin credentials; seeding occurs only when no admin user is present (or an equivalent safe, non-destructive policy).
Passwords are not stored in plaintext in stable state (store a hash or equivalent secure representation).

requirements.text: Update the frontend sign-in experience so an administrator can log in using the seeded credentials (username "Rushikesh", password "123") via the existing username/password authentication flow (not Internet Identity), and ensure all user-facing login text remains in English.

quotes: make Admin username  as - Rushikesh Passoword - 123

acceptanceCriteria: The Login page provides a username/password sign-in path that works with username "Rushikesh" and password "123".
After successful login as the seeded Admin, the UI reflects Admin permissions (e.g., Admin route access is granted).
All login page labels, helper text, and error messages are in English.

constraints: Backend must remain a single Motoko actor with all logic in backend/main.mo; only add backend/migration.mo changes if needed to preserve/upgrade stable state safely.

Do not edit files under frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.tsx, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, or any files under frontend/src/components/ui (compose instead).
nonGoals: Implementing third-party authentication providers (only supported auth mechanisms are Internet Identity and in-app username/password).
Adding password reset email/SMS flows or external integrations.
Changing post/content features unrelated to setting the default Admin credentials.
